    Boundary subspaces for string detectors #

    For a Butler--Ringel endpoint word C, the lower subspace C^- starts with the image of the unique compatible incoming arrow, or zero if there is none. The upper subspace C^+ starts with the kernel of the unique compatible outgoing arrow, or the whole source space if there is none. Both are then transported along C.

    The polarization selects the correct one of the at most two arrows at a trivial endpoint. For a nontrivial word the same sign condition is forced by string composability. This file proves the fundamental inclusion C^-(M) <= C^+(M) and its naturality under module morphisms.
